_readme: Locale coverage policy + native-review status. Consumed by scripts/check-i18n.mjs.
gated:   locales that MUST be 100% complete. Any missing key or missing CLDR
plural category fails CI. Add a locale here only when it is fully
translated AND we intend to ship it to a client — promoting a locale
means every future PR that adds a UI string must translate it too.
baseline: which keys each non-gated locale currently RESOLVES, as coverage
ids. An id is `some.key`, or `some.key#few` for one CLDR plural
category of a plural key. NOTE: this tracks key presence only —
it does NOT mean the value is in the target language. Many backlog
values are still English. Only gated locales are value-checked.
The rule is a one-way ratchet: losing any id listed here FAILS CI.
Adding a new English string does NOT fail these locales — it widens
a backlog we already accept and will fill before that language is
presented to anyone.
So a PR owes English + every `gated` locale, and nothing else.
Regenerate with: node scripts/check-i18n.mjs --update-baseline
These lists should only ever grow.
sameAsEnglish: keys whose value is allowed to be identical to en.json in a
GATED locale. For gated locales the checker also fails on any value
left byte-identical to English, because key presence alone is a weak
signal — a copy of en.json would otherwise report 100% complete while
rendering an entirely English UI. Add a key here only when the English
form is genuinely correct in that language: a symbol, a brand name, a
resource code. Never add one just to silence the check.
This rule applies to gated locales only; backlog locales are full of
untranslated values by definition and are governed by `baseline`.
The list is currently GLOBAL across gated locales. Only `ar` is
gated today; before gating a second locale, decide whether these
exemptions are right for it too, or make the list per-locale.
i18n-apply.mjs also refuses to --overwrite an allow-listed key.
review:  native-speaker review status per locale. `machine-drafted` means the
strings were produced by an AI and have had NO native pass — do not
present that language to a client until this says otherwise. Record
a native pass by moving the locale to `reviewed` with the date.

en.note: Source of truth; authored in English.

ar.note: Fully translated: every key present and every value in Arabic, apart from the 20 allow-listed brand/code/symbol strings in sameAsEnglish. Two AI-drafted waves on 2026-08-10 — 443 missing keys (books/setup/import/layout/preferences/topbar + misc, all six CLDR plural categories), then 189 values that had been left as English text (preferences, templates, setup, pipeline, workspace), including 5 holding stale English from a superseded en.json wording. Both waves were drafted against the existing ar.json for terminology consistency and validated for placeholder preservation and bidi cleanliness. NATIVE REVIEW STILL PENDING — no Arabic speaker has read any of it.
